batch_strategy: Select 32 experiments that test loading-qualified structural transfer, fill missing ratio-response segments, and resolve one concrete reproducibility problem. Use the latest feedback to prioritize donor-response interactions and endpoint-specific learning, while extending coverage into amino compounds, carbonyl baselines, aromatic ethers, and a nonpolar halide boundary.

choices.reason: Repeat m73's 52.45 mg pure-EA condition, currently predicted at 18.01/22.51 mL. Observed 3d5a3094cb10eee37b37 recorded 21.83/21.35, with completion preceding onset. Replication tests label stability and endpoint ordering before this unusual baseline is transferred across loading or ratio.

m73 in pure EA at 104.9 mg predicts 18.01/22.52 mL, almost identical to the lower-loading forecast. Compare with the selected lower-loading repeat and measured 1/1 record 2cf789c87f7c6325c020 at 18.60/18.96. This tests whether late stronger-eluent endpoints extend beyond the problematic lower-loading records.

m73 at 2/1 and 52.45 mg predicts 7.05/11.48 mL. It supplies a missing exact-injection anchor following the late pure-EA and repeated 1/1 records 3d5a3094cb10eee37b37, 7bd4e959319ef8b7b0fe, and a387411cbcb6be48bde4. The label distinguishes a loading-specific transition from transfer of the measured middle-loading 2/1 response.

Methoxyphenethyl alcohol m119 at 2/1 and 52.9 mg predicts 20.35/31.01 mL. Middle-loading record 17c1bb3be086a2b6ffec measured 20.00/31.61 under otherwise matching conditions. After m120's sharply different loading responses, this tests whether the related molecule with an extra methylene preserves the forecast loading invariance.

m119 at 1/1 and 158.7 mg predicts 11.83/19.24 mL. Together with the selected matched 2/1 row, it fills the early segment between pure-EA observation 3f5051191caf6ab07337 and 5/1 observation e6e78489d1da4066c07e. The baseline separates a loading difference already present at 1/1 from one appearing between ratios.

m119 at matched 2/1 and 158.7 mg predicts 20.34/31.03 mL. Comparison with the selected 52.9 mg row and measured 105.8 mg record 17c1bb3be086a2b6ffec tests nearly identical forecasts across loading. This qualifies transfer of m120's newly demonstrated loading-dependent early response to another methoxy-alcohol connectivity.

Dibenzoylmethane m168 at 20/1, 80 mg, and 400 uL DCM predicts 6.22/23.68 mL. The otherwise matched 300 uL observation 07a069e105eb7739bf7e measured 5.26/22.36. The latest 5/1 volume comparison ea810ad3e836415369bd versus 5ab2073d8b67153b8455 showed a small completion difference and identical onset; this single extension tests whether that weak volume association persists at a different ratio.

Para-aminobenzonitrile m160 at 5/1 and 50 mg predicts 40.52/98.18 mL. Middle- and higher-loading records b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 and fe66b2381d33aa2ea3a8 establish a late response. Paired with the selected meta isomer at identical recorded conditions, this tests whether the isomer-specific onset/completion relationship persists at lower loading.

Lactone m181 in pure EA at 58.45 mg predicts 4.89/18.30 mL. The selected matched 2/1 forecast has shorter completion, while measured 5/1 and 10/1 records fd327bd31cbab5b296a7 and 2cc7c8ae52cdb25ca284 show substantial later growth. This establishes an uncovered baseline in a cyclic ester environment and tests the predicted early completion decrease.

m181 at matched 2/1 and 58.45 mg predicts 5.44/14.71 mL. It connects the selected pure-EA baseline to measured 5/1 record fd327bd31cbab5b296a7 at 11.46/18.46 and 10/1 record 2cc7c8ae52cdb25ca284 at 21.45/31.79. The pair locates the early transition separately for onset and completion.

Bis-benzoyl compound m178 in pure EA at 116.5 mg predicts 3.46/12.59 mL. Its measured 5/1 and 10/1 records 17ff889395addf7d6295 and 634f21e11a8442494ce3 retain early onset while completion grows. With the selected 1/1 row, this supplies missing early labels for a two-carbonyl topology whose later response becomes much steeper.

m178 at matched 1/1 predicts 3.79/10.37 mL, below its pure-EA completion forecast. The pair determines whether this modest early completion decrease resembles measured m179 records a2c075159f93cc78c444 and 593cfb8dc5f3c8b36cac or is another prediction artifact. It anchors structural transfer before m178's measured weak-eluent transition.

Naphthyl ketone m40 at 50/1 and 168 mg predicts 34.12/57.97 mL. Measured middle-loading c2334ccf8e6788ac6ca2 was 38.80/67.99 after a substantial acquisition-time underprediction; the latest middle-loading 20/1 label b645df00945e594953a6 was much closer to forecast. This tests loading transfer specifically in the repaired weak-eluent extension.

Methoxybenzaldehyde m118 at 5/1 and 168.15 mg predicts 8.06/20.80 mL. It connects higher-loading 2/1 observation 4e7e45a513ce579c5ce3 to middle-loading 5/1 observation 98586ac2d6d266ddb78c at 12.88/20.30. The label tests whether loading changes onset more than completion before the endpoint decoupling measured at 10/1.

Alpha-ketoester m92 at 2/1 and 173.25 mg predicts 7.02/14.08 mL. Lower- and middle-loading observations 9768d61b571fc0c5ce1a and f7d6c68ef2b3f637bd05 differ in completion, while the latest lower-loading 1/1 repeat reproduced its earlier anchor closely. This completes the 2/1 loading comparison without imposing smooth interpolation.

m92 at 5/1 and 115.5 mg predicts 9.31/23.23 mL. Lower-loading 790d27f0fa045d91f307 measured 8.61/21.06 and higher-loading 6c1c34b12c66ebcf39a4 measured 7.14/27.72. The missing middle loading tests separate onset and completion associations and connects its stronger-eluent loading behavior to later measured ratios.

Ether-containing beta-ketoester m107 in pure EA at 109 mg predicts 6.36/15.82 mL. Lower-loading pure-EA d76d74e2a624a532f9f8 measured 6.23/15.73, while matched middle-loading 1/1 record 60b7eed7a46a03b366b2 measured 10.82/27.16. This missing baseline tests loading invariance before the much larger, loading-qualified 2/1 and 5/1 responses.

Multifunctional ester-ketone m13 at 5/1 and 56.1 mg predicts 19.17/42.33 mL. Middle- and higher-loading records a421784c91de559c18e0 and 5d530b2f228ed39ff952 have earlier onset at higher loading but similar completion; recent 10/1 record ca467c94f14b2219503e preserves that endpoint distinction. This missing lower-loading anchor tests the extent of the association.

Para-aminoacetophenone m36 at 1/1 and 38.5 mg predicts 9.68/21.72 mL. With the selected matched 2/1 row, it measures an uncovered early slope in an amino-ketone environment. Middle-loading 2/1 observation 6b7209c2e8154837a8c7 was much later than its acquisition forecast, motivating qualification of the now-steep predicted response across loading.

m36 at matched 2/1 predicts 22.78/41.90 mL. Compare with the selected 1/1 baseline and measured 77 mg 2/1 record 6b7209c2e8154837a8c7 at 22.32/39.86. This tests whether the early steep transition transfers to lower loading and supplies an amino-ketone boundary for the selected amino-ester conditions.

Para-amino benzoate m86 at 1/1 and 175.5 mg predicts 7.72/16.45 mL. Its matched measured 2/1 record 073e6abf4d3bfffc2761 was 10.57/22.67 and 5/1 record 9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb was 26.80/57.07. This missing early anchor tests where the ester environment begins its pronounced retention growth.

m86 at 2/1 and 117 mg predicts 12.21/25.51 mL. Higher-loading 073e6abf4d3bfffc2761 measured 10.57/22.67, while both measured 5/1 loadings finish much later. This supplies the missing middle-loading 2/1 anchor and qualifies transfer of the amino-ketone's steeper early response to an amino-ester.

Beta-enaminoester m72 at 1/1, 51.1 mg, and 300 uL PE predicts 6.51/20.81 mL. With the selected matched PE 2/1 row, it fills the early response before measured 5/1 record bdfa3c592507c0609ee1. The latest PE weak-eluent labels support steep later growth, making the uncovered baseline informative for locating the transition.

m72 at 2/1 and 51.1 mg with 200 uL DCM predicts 9.03/24.31 mL. Compare with the selected PE/300 uL 2/1 condition and measured DCM 5/1 record 10f01f359bc6067d009f. This tests early transfer between complete recorded injection tuples; the comparison cannot isolate a solvent-only effect because volume also changes.

m72 at 2/1 and 51.1 mg with 300 uL PE predicts 9.05/24.29 mL, within 0.03 mL per endpoint of the selected DCM forecast. Measured PE/DCM differences at 5/1 and 20/1 are endpoint- and ratio-dependent. With the selected matched PE 1/1 row, this simultaneously measures an early slope and tests model insensitivity to the joint injection conditions.

Trimethoxybenzene m110 at 10/1 and 112.6 mg predicts 5.63/16.53 mL, below its matched 5/1 forecast. No measured matched segment establishes that dip. Paired with 20/1 and anchored by measured 50/1 record ce39d1762993bbbafaca, this tests the missing transition in an aromatic-ether environment.

m110 at matched 20/1 predicts 10.64/20.47 mL. The selected 10/1-to-20/1 segment connects to ce39d1762993bbbafaca at 22.94/36.12 and distinguishes gradual growth from a later sharp rise. Comparison with dimethoxybenzene observations remains loading-qualified and can teach which aromatic-ether slopes transfer.

Anisole m126 at 20/1 and 49.75 mg predicts 9.65/15.67 mL. Together with matched 50/1, it measures a missing weak-eluent slope; observed b1737f3e487bbd039406 anchors 5/1 at 99.5 mg. This tests transfer from measured dimethoxy and trimethoxy curves while keeping the selected pair internally matched.

m126 at matched 50/1 predicts 13.84/23.67 mL. The pair tests whether a single aryl ether develops the forecast later onset and completion, relative to qualified dimethoxy reference a47a3987d45e7c542d38 and trimethoxy reference ce39d1762993bbbafaca. High CW distance is supplementary coverage evidence, not proof of prediction error.

Iodotoluene m140 at 50/1 and 100 mg predicts 11.32/14.88 mL, compared with measured 20/1 record b9529a88ac5b822de9c4 at 5.52/10.14. This tests an uncovered nonpolar weak-eluent onset change against qualified chlorotoluene and dimethyliodobenzene references. It provides a boundary check relevant to many halogenated low-polarity rows; CW percentile 1.0 is secondary evidence.

Diphenyl sulfoxide m199 at 2/1 and 150 mg predicts 13.61/25.54 mL. Lower-loading 9ddc2e8babb52ee8e772 measured 14.26/26.03, and lower-loading 5/1 record f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c was substantially later. This tests whether early loading invariance extends to a sulfoxide oxygen environment, qualifying transfer of carbonyl-centered loading relationships.

Meta-aminobenzonitrile m161 at 5/1 and 50 mg predicts 27.58/82.50 mL. Middle- and higher-loading records 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e and 3774a4dac6dd0f01d48d provide anchors. With the selected para isomer at identical conditions, this closes a lower-loading structural comparison and tests the forecast isomer difference separately for onset and completion.

hypotheses.content: Methoxy-alcohol response cannot be transferred as a generally shallow curve or a loading-independent slope. m120's 55.65 mg response rises strongly through 5/1, whereas its higher-loading 2/1 response is much earlier. Whether the extra methylene in m119 preserves its forecast common loading response remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest large donor-response miss exposes a structure-by-ratio-by-loading interaction. The m119 panel tests its transfer boundary instead of applying an unrestricted OH correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1, do lower and higher m119 loadings remain close to the measured middle loading, and does the higher-loading 1/1-to-2/1 segment remain steep?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading associations are endpoint-, structure-, and ratio-dependent. m92's repeated lower-loading 1/1 baseline is comparatively stable, while other loadings differ strongly in completion. m94's completed 20/1 loading series supports a larger onset than completion association, and m107's measured 1/1 baseline is more similar across loading than its later response. These observations do not establish a causal or universal loading law.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Missing loading anchors identify where nearly invariant forecasts are appropriate and where onset and completion need different responses. The sulfoxide singleton tests transfer beyond ester and ketone oxygen environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m92's missing loading anchors preserve its endpoint-specific associations, and do m107 and m199 retain similar early baselines across loading?

hypotheses.content: m73 repeatedly has late recorded stronger-eluent endpoints, but the stability and physical interpretation of its compact response remain unresolved. The exact 1/1 repeat differs materially from the earlier record, and both latest pure-EA and 1/1 labels have V2 below V1. These endpoint-order inconsistencies require a reproducibility test and should not be assigned an adsorption mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A stable unusual recorded association and unstable endpoint labels imply different limits on deterministic prediction. One exact repeat plus adjacent-condition anchors can constrain inappropriate transfer of this region.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the lower-loading pure-EA record reproduce with consistent endpoint ordering, is its late baseline present at middle loading, and where does the lower-loading 2/1 response lie?

hypotheses.content: At m168's tested 5/1 condition, changing DCM loading volume from 300 to 400 uL left recorded onset unchanged and changed completion by about 1.21 mL. This supports only a small association at that condition; volume invariance across the ratio-response curve remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: One 20/1 extension tests whether the small observed volume association persists into a different retention regime, without allocating another full volume-response panel.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 80 mg and 20/1, does the 400 uL DCM label remain close to the measured 300 uL endpoints?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl connectivity and structural environment qualify both the early baseline and weak-eluent slope. m175 preserves early onset with modest weak-eluent completion growth, m40 rises substantially, and m118 exhibits onset/completion decoupling. m179's measured early completion decrease is modest, far smaller than its former forecast. The uncovered m181 and m178 baselines cannot be inferred reliably from a shared carbonyl offset.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The baseline pairs teach missing early regimes for cyclic ester and multiple-carbonyl topologies. The m40 and m118 extensions test loading-qualified transfer of measured endpoint-specific responses.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m181 and m178 reproduce the forecast early completion decreases, and do m40 and m118 preserve their measured response relationships at the selected higher loadings?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen environment and aromatic substitution affect where endpoint growth emerges, with loading qualifying transfer. Dibenzylamine's lower and middle loadings are close at 2/1 but diverge strongly at 5/1. Amino-ketone, amino-ester, and amino-nitrile observations also show different onset/completion relationships. The para/meta amino-nitrile difference is observed at two loading levels, but its lower-loading extension remains a prediction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Early condition anchors distinguish amino-carbonyl environments without reducing them to nitrogen counts. The amino-nitrile pair tests a structural boundary at identical recorded conditions and fills missing loading coverage.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the amino-ketone develop its steeper early onset growth at lower loading, where does the amino-ester transition begin, and does the amino-nitrile isomer difference persist at 50 mg?

hypotheses.content: m72's steep completion growth transfers into the measured PE/300 uL response, but endpoint differences between PE/300 uL and DCM/200 uL are ratio-dependent and confounded by the simultaneous volume change. Repeated lower-loading 10/1 DCM records also disagree substantially. The nearly identical current early forecasts across injection tuples are untested model behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected PE early slope and joint-injection comparison locate the transition before the measured steep region. They qualify condition transfer while acknowledging record variability.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 51.1 mg, do the 2/1 PE/300 uL and DCM/200 uL endpoints agree, and what internally matched PE 1/1-to-2/1 slope precedes the later growth?

hypotheses.content: The uncovered weak-eluent response of m110 may develop differently from the single- and double-methoxy aromatic ethers. Its measured 50/1 endpoints are later than the supplied dimethoxy reference, although loading differs. Its predicted intermediate onset dip and anisole's predicted weak-eluent growth remain unmeasured. Methoxy count alone does not establish transferable slopes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two internally matched ratio-response pairs fill sparse aromatic-ether segments and test whether local model shapes transfer across substitution patterns. These rows extend learning beyond the repeatedly studied polar failure families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m110 retain early onset at 10/1 before rising at 20/1, and how does anisole's measured 20/1-to-50/1 slope compare with the loading-qualified dimethoxy and trimethoxy references?

feedback_interpretation: The latest m120 outcomes reject the forecast lower-loading decrease toward 5/1: the label was 50.73/71.53 mL versus the acquisition forecast of 13.70/18.78. The higher-loading 2/1 label, 8.02/10.83, also rejects transfer of the lower-loading steep early segment, despite similar measured 1/1 baselines. I therefore test loading-qualified transfer in m119 rather than retain a general shallow methoxy-alcohol hypothesis. The m73 results make the earlier compact-band interpretation less secure: its exact 1/1 repeat changed materially, and both new stronger-eluent records have V2 below V1. This motivates one exact pure-EA repeat and surrounding anchors, without asserting a mechanism or discarding the records. The m168 volume pair recorded identical onset and only a 1.21 mL completion difference, reducing priority for extensive volume experiments; one weaker-eluent extension tests the scope of that result. The latest m40 20/1, m175 weak-eluent pair, m182 5/1, and m118 early labels were comparatively close to their acquisition forecasts. These outcomes support endpoint-specific carbonyl distinctions and reduce the value of repeating those covered segments. m179's extended pure-EA completion forecast was largely rejected, although a modest measured decrease to 1/1 remains; new baseline experiments therefore test specific missing topologies without enforcing monotonicity. m94's completed loading series and m107's higher-loading 1/1 label support their respective endpoint-specific association and shared early baseline. m92's lower-loading 1/1 repeat was close to the earlier measurement, supporting use of that anchor for missing loading comparisons. Dibenzylamine's new lower-loading 2/1 label is close to the middle-loading reference, localizing its larger loading divergence farther along the curve. The new PE m72 pair supports steep later completion growth but leaves the early injection-tuple response unresolved. All errors discussed here are historical acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals; c6924324ddd95f249df6 is correctly treated as m107.
batch_rationale: This corrected batch contains exactly 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs and no pending experiments. Its failure-driven component addresses transfer of the newly exposed donor loading interaction, together with a targeted reproducibility test for m73. Loading selections connect to measured anchors and distinguish onset associations from completion associations; stable baselines are useful learning outcomes as well as departures from model invariance. Carbonyl selections concentrate on uncovered stronger-eluent regimes and loading-qualified extensions after the latest feedback reduced the need to remeasure repaired middle segments. The amino-compound anchors and matched amino-nitrile isomers probe nitrogen connectivity and substitution boundaries with nearby measured references. The m72 panel tests an early PE ratio slope and transfer between complete recorded injection tuples, explicitly preserving solvent/volume confounding. Aromatic-ether pairs and the iodotoluene extension cover missing relationships relevant to numerous less-polar rows. Selected ratio-response pairs hold density, sample volume, loading-solvent identity, and loading-solvent volume fixed; cross-loading comparisons are identified separately. The sole exact replicate matches a previously observed m73 tuple, and no two selected rows have identical molecule-plus-condition tuples. These labels may improve overall Row V1/V2 accuracy by constraining transferable slopes, structural boundaries, recorded loading interactions, and regions where label variability limits deterministic prediction. The plan does not optimize the selected separations or seek maximal retention. Loading amount is the density-times-volume feature, and no absent concentration, pH, flow, or column variables are assumed. Quantile spans and CW distances are supplementary evidence rather than calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Elution interval width is distinct from prediction uncertainty, and m73's endpoint-order inconsistencies are treated explicitly.
